facts.text: Mountain City was originally called Pass Over because a road crossed the continental divide, and it sits about 2,500 feet above sea level.
The Georgia General Assembly incorporated the town as Pass Over in 1907, and it was renamed Mountain City in 1915 to reflect its elevated position.
Tallulah Falls Railroad’s depot in Mountain City once had a roof that burned, but the granite walls kept the building standing.
The York House, built in 1896 as Georgia’s oldest bed‑and‑breakfast, hosted Walt Disney and Joel Chandler Harris and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982.
The Mountain City Playhouse, famous for its weekend square‑dancing nights, has been a local cultural hub for decades.
